sm: John Stossel examines California's high-speed rail project, promised as a train running at up to two hundred twenty miles per hour between Los Angeles and San Francisco in about two and a half hours. After eighteen years and fifteen billion dollars, he says no track has been laid, and the estimated cost has grown from thirty-three billion to one hundred twenty-six billion dollars. Officials now plan only a Merced to Bakersfield link through farm country, costing thirty-six billion dollars and possibly opening in 2033. He notes that promised private investors have not come forward, and that the project's boss and staff spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on luxury and late night rides, after which the boss resigned. He says other countries have built fast trains and blames California's environmental lawsuits, union work rules, bad management and weak oversight.
